transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... well, I guess the regular clinic doctor told me I needed to come in. They kind of got on me about my eating. But I just... I keep things simple. Just coffee in the morning, and maybe a few bites of something between painting jobs. And then a small dinner, if I'm not too busy with my class paperwork. So... yeah, that's why I'm here.
Do you choose to eat this way or do you often not feel like eating?
Um... I don't know. I'm not really sure. I guess I just... I don't really think about it that much. It's just what I'm used to doing.
Do you enjoy eating when you do eat?
Um... I don't really know. I guess I don't really think of it like that. It's just... food. I don't really pay much attention to whether I enjoy it or not.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

Um... I guess some weight, yeah. My work pants are hanging pretty loose lately. People on the job sites keep making comments... saying I look too thin. But I just... I feel like I've just leaned out, you know? From being on my feet all day painting and doing wallpaper. It's an active job.
Are you worried about gaining weight?

Um... I don't know if worried is the right word. It's just... if I eat something heavy, like pizza or a big sandwich or something... I get this... kind of panicky feeling. Like I'll wake up bigger, and... just slower. I need to be able to move around ladders and tight rooms for my job, so... I just can't afford to be weighed down like that.
How often do you think about the possibility of gaining weight?
Um... I'm not really sure. I don't keep track of it or anything. Just... sometimes, I guess.
Do you fear gaining weight?

I mean... like I was just saying, I guess. It's just... that panicky feeling I mentioned. If I have something heavy, like a sandwich or whatever. I just... I don't want to wake up bigger. I have to be able to get up and down the ladders for work, so... yeah. I guess I'm afraid of it slowing me down.
Do you think you would still limit your food intake even if you weren't working a physically demanding job?
I don't know. Um... I've been doing this kind of work for a long time, so... I haven't really thought about it.
Do you think you would look bad if you gained weight?

I don't know about looking bad... it's more just... like I said, if I eat something heavy, like pizza or that sandwich, I just get that panicky feeling. I just... I can't wake up bigger. I need to be able to move around the rooms and up and down the ladders the way I need to. I just can't be slower.
Do you think your weight or body shape is important to how you feel about yourself?

Um... I don't really know. I don't think about it like that. I just... I feel fine as long as I can do my work. It's not really about... how I feel about myself, I guess. I just need to be able to do my job.
Do you think you would still want to be as thin as you are now even if it didn't affect your job performance?
I don't really know. Um... it's hard to separate the two, I guess. I just... I've always done this kind of work, so I haven't really pictured it any other way.
Is your main reason for limiting your food intake because you are afraid of gaining weight?

I mean... I guess so. It's just... like I was saying before, if I eat something heavy, I just get this panic. Like... I'll wake up bigger, and then I won't be able to move around the ladders as easily. So... yeah, I guess I am afraid of that.
Do you think you would be upset if you gained weight just because of how you would look?
I don't know. Um... I try not to look in the mirror very much, honestly. So... I'm not really sure if it's about how I look. I just... I just don't want it to happen.
Would you want to avoid gaining weight even if nobody else would notice?
I guess... yeah. I just... I wouldn't want it to happen. It wouldn't really matter if anyone else saw it or not. I'd still know.
Is your fear of gaining weight because you don't want to look a certain way?
Um... I don't really know. Like I said before, I don't really look at myself much. So... I don't think it's about a specific look. I just... I just don't want the weight there.
Would your fear of gaining weight change if you knew you could gain weight without changing your appearance?

Um... probably not. It's... it's more about how it feels, I guess. Like, if I eat something heavy, like a big sandwich or pizza... I just get this panicky feeling. Like I'll wake up bigger and... just slower. I paint houses for a living, so... I have to move around ladders and tight rooms all day. I just... I need to be able to move the way I need to. So, yeah... I still wouldn't want it.
Is your fear of gaining weight because of how it would make you feel about your body?
I'm... not really sure. I don't think so. It's just... I just don't want it.
Is your fear of gaining weight more about how it would affect your body's ability to function or how it would affect your self-image?

I think... I mean, I kind of just said it. It's the functioning part, mostly. Like I mentioned, if I eat something heavy... pizza or whatever... I just get panicked that I'll wake up bigger. And slower. I need to be able to move around the ladders and the rooms for work. I just... I need my body to work right. Not feel weighed down.
Is your fear of gaining weight mostly about how your body would look or how it would perform physically?

I... I feel like I just answered that. It's about performing physically. Like I said... if I eat a big sandwich or something, I just panic that I'll wake up bigger and won't be able to get up and down the ladders. I just need to be able to move for my job. That's all.
Do you think your eating habits are more related to your physical needs for work or to thoughts and feelings about food and your body?
I don't know... I feel like we just keep going over this. It's the work thing. I don't really have all these deep thoughts and feelings about it... I just want to be able to do my job.
